title: Vaginal Bleeding

rationale.Physical Exam: Abdomen: Assess for pelvic mass or tenderness.
rationale.Physical Exam: Genitalia / Pelvic / Spec: Visualize source of bleeding. Bimanual exam for uterine size, adnexal masses.
rationale.HCG, beta (pregnancy test): MUST rule out pregnancy — ectopic, miscarriage, molar pregnancy can all present with vaginal bleeding.
rationale.CBC with differential: Assess degree of anemia from blood loss. Platelet count.
rationale.TSH / Prolactin: Thyroid dysfunction and hyperprolactinemia cause anovulatory bleeding.
rationale.PT/PTT / INR: Screen for coagulopathy (von Willebrand disease can present with menorrhagia).
rationale.Pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal): Rule out fibroids, polyps, adenomyosis, ovarian masses. Assess endometrial thickness.
rationale.Endometrial biopsy: Indicated if age >45, unopposed estrogen exposure, or risk factors for endometrial hyperplasia/cancer.
rationale.BMP / CMP / LFTs: Screening labs. Iron studies if anemic.
rationale.Combined oral contraceptives: Hormonal regulation. Estrogen-progestin combination stabilizes endometrium and regulates cycles.
rationale.Iron supplementation: Treat iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss.
rationale.Hysterectomy as first-line: DUB responds to medical management (OCPs, cyclic progestins). Surgery reserved for failed medical therapy or completed childbearing.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a reproductive-age woman presenting with irregular, heavy vaginal bleeding without identifiable structural or systemic cause. This is dysfunctional uterine bleeding (DUB), most commonly anovulatory — unopposed estrogen stimulation leads to endometrial hyperplasia and irregular shedding. Diagnosis of exclusion after ruling out pregnancy, structural lesions (fibroids, polyps), thyroid dysfunction, coagulopathy, and malignancy. Workup: HCG (rule out pregnancy/complications), CBC (assess anemia from blood loss), TSH/prolactin, pelvic ultrasound (rule out structural causes), endometrial biopsy if age >45 or risk factors. Treatment depends on severity and fertility goals: hormonal regulation with combined OCPs or cyclic progestins. If acute heavy bleeding: high-dose estrogen or IV conjugated estrogens. Iron supplementation for anemia.
